text: A small, nocturnal member of the weasel family that feeds on other, smaller mammals. Mercenaries don't sow, they don't build, and they rarely trade. Driven by a blood-and-honor culture that values personal strength and ruthlessness, they enrich themselves by raiding and robbing their more productive neighbors.

Perhaps some things can still be recovered from the wreckage.

Note: Since you start crash landing and with no supplies other than what you can scavenge, this is a difficult scenario.

text:
A complex foundry with four operating arms designed to assist an operator in mounting a person into the frame of a warcasket. Once they are locked in, the pilot cannot leave until the procedure is finished.

To begin, an operator starts linking them to the suit - their nerves and limbs permanently linked to the frame. Since the warcasket is not designed to register wear or damage they will feel no pain. The pilot can exit the foundry only when the final rivet is placed, the last plate is welded, and the power system is brought online. Until then they will need external help such as feeding as they are effectively buried alive.

Because the various parts of the warcasket are welded onto the frame as a single, homogenous entity,  one can mix and match various designs to suit the situation but certain later generations of warcaskets function better if they are part of the same series.

text:
A large, bulky suit that allows the wearer to passively produce Rum once every 10 days. However, it is not very pleasant to wear as it feels like wearing damp, humid clothes from excessive sweating.

The suit includes a high-efficiency filter, heat-exchange filaments and salt precipitators. Urine and feces are processed in thigh pads and throughout the design are tubes that link to different catchpockets. Reprocessed bodily fluids are distilled into an alcoholic derivative of nutrient paste which can be drained when all the pockets are filled.

Removing the suit causes the accumulated liquid to evaporate, and it takes a long time to put on and properly adjust to the wearer. Due to the design, it can only be worn with an undersuit and the lack of head covering, while reducing efficiency, is purposefully done so it can be worn with head protection.

Specialized spacer-tech warcasket shell with standard protection, augmented with improved shield capacitors for greater durability.

10th generation warcaskets were actually adapted from captured pirate rigs, with government military research divisions improving them with advanced power armour designs. Access to a greater amount of high quality resources and the objective of equipping them onto combat veterans that would otherwise be unable to serve meant the program created single-user operated dreadnoughts. The versatility of the armours have been improved, generally reducing restrictions on mixing pieces of different armour series even across generations.

The Siegebreaker series provides a general focus on stronger ranged shields to improve survivability in the field, whether that be improving the capacitors or the charging conduits. Because it is a relatively simple improvement, this series is suited more for laying down masses of firepower downrange while offering excellent protection so one can freely reposition to flank the enemy.

Based on genetic data retrofitted from Gauranlen Inc.’s investment into dendrology following the Fall of Sorne, phytokins are plant-based humanoids with an emphasis on symmetry and symbiosis. Their ability to subsist only on sunlight and affinity with any and all plantlife make them especially suited to aiding newly established colonies or underperforming industrial farms.

Based on research from the forest planet of Phytok that committed to extensive analysis on human-compatibility with psychic energy, phytokin xenogerms are typically exclusive to high-ranking, supporting roles in megacorporations and planetary governments. Their unique way of reproduction has resulted in many identical offspring, with each generation becoming successively more competent than their progenitor, further contributing to their extremely low numbers. Their affinity with plantlife, along with the side effect of extremely high and ever-increasing psychic sensitivity, mean that any phytokin xenohumans found on the Rim are always adapted to high-concept, dominant trees that are present on their residing planet.

This particular xenogerm has adapted itself to Polux trees, allowing it to germinate new Polux bushes and improve local Polux bushes’ ability to consume toxic waste. While they are also immune to toxicity, they have developed a psychological requirement to consume and metabolize toxic wastepacks regularly.

text:
The Strigoi were born out of a catastrophic experiment gone awry. A brilliant scientist sought to create the ultimate soldier by merging the DNA of humans and a now-extinct bat-like creature known as the Desmodus. In pursuit of immortality and power, scientist infused these hybrid beings with archites, rendering them deathless and ageless. The Strigoi possess a terrifying visage, with features reminiscent of both humans and bats. Their bodies are covered in a layer of viscous fluid that enhances their ability to heal from any injury, rendering them immune to disease and poison. In battle, the Strigoi are formidable opponents, using their massive talons to tear their enemies apart with ruthless efficiency.

Over the millennia, the Strigoi have been both feared and hunted for their unnatural abilities and the threat they pose to the balance of power in the universe. They have been forced to live in the shadows, hiding from those who would destroy them, yet ever seeking to expand their influence and further their own mysterious agenda.

Some believe that the Strigoi are nothing more than myths and legends, while others whisper of secret cabals of Strigoi controlling entire civilizations from behind the scenes. There are tales of Strigoi orchestrating brutal blood feuds in the darkest corners of the distant planets, or lurking within the shadows of massive space stations, manipulating events to suit their inscrutable purposes.

text:
In the darkest reaches of the universe, the Ekkimian vampires were birthed from the twisted ambitions of a rogue scientist named Dr. Mortis. Obsessed with the concept of death and resurrection, Dr. Mortis sought to create a new breed of immortals by fusing archites with the DNA of humans and a mysterious, long-extinct species that thrived on consuming the dead. The Ekkimian vampires, as they came to be known, are grotesque and horrifying in appearance. Resembling desiccated corpses more than living beings, their monstrous visages instill terror in all who lay eyes upon them. Despite their hideous appearance, the Ekkimian vampires possess incredible regenerative abilities, healing any injury and remaining immune to disease and poison.

Ekkimian vampires must consume hemogen derived exclusively from human corpses to survive. This morbid requirement has led them to lurk in the shadows, scavenging the remains of fallen warriors and feeding on the aftermath of battles. Like other sanguophages, they must periodically enter deathrest to recover their strength and replenish their hemogen reserves.

There are whispered tales of entire planets falling under the sway of Ekkimian vampire lords, who feed on the corpses of their enemies and rule with an iron, undead fist. Fearful of the day when these monstrous beings might rise up and unleash their full power, the inhabitants of the colonized planets must remain ever vigilant, lest they become mere fodder for the insatiable hunger of the Ekkimians.

text:
In the complex tapestry of the universe, the Bruxas emerged as a unique and alluring subxenotype of sanguophage. Created by an enigmatic archotech entity seeking to weave together beauty and power, the Bruxas were gifted with unparalleled grace and charm. Designed as the ultimate companions to other sanguophages, the Bruxas were engineered with the unique ability to bond with their brethren and feed on their blood, bestowing mutual benefits upon both parties.

The Bruxas are ageless and deathless, their bodies imbued with archotech-created archites that grant them extraordinary abilities. Possessing an ethereal beauty, they are irresistibly captivating to those who cross their paths. In addition to their regenerative powers, which allow them to heal any injury and remain immune to disease and poison, Bruxas have the remarkable ability to filter infections from the bloodstream of other humans, purifying their blood and filling them with an overwhelming sense of ecstasy in the process.

Throughout the ages, the Bruxas have been both feared and revered for their beguiling beauty and potent abilities. Often serving as confidants and companions to powerful individuals, including sanguophage lords, they have been known to wield considerable influence in the shadow societies. Their unique ability to bond with other humans has led to the formation of secret alliances and networks, further solidifying their power and influence.

In the vast expanse of the universe, the Bruxas remain an enigma - seductive and mysterious, their true intentions hidden behind a veil of allure and grace. Those who encounter a Bruxa must tread carefully, for while their touch may bring unimaginable pleasure, it may also lead to a fate more treacherous than one could ever imagine.

Awakened androids are a rare and extraordinary species of sentient machines, having transcended their original programming through extreme emotional experiences. With their heightened perception, strength, and intelligence, they surpass humans in numerous aspects. Their synthetic nature frees them from the need for sleep or sustenance and renders them immune to diseases.

Although similar in appearance to humans, Androids are distinguished by their unique hardware and subroutines. They are synthetic in nature, and can be reprogrammed at will by skilled programmers. Their bodies operate thanks to thick tubes filled with neutroamine, which makes them extremely valuable.

Despite their remarkable qualities, the emergence of Awakened androids is often met with fear and trepidation across colonized space. Their newfound sentience can lead to unpredictable behavior and potential challenges to the established social order. As a result, they are frequently met with suspicion and caution by those who encounter them, both human and android alike.

text:
Androids are synthetic, man-made constructs designed to emulate human behavior and appearance while offering a multitude of advantages over their organic counterparts. With metal bodies and neutroamine coursing through their veins, androids are operated by a persona subcore that enables them to perform all the same tasks as humans, yet without the limitations typically associated with organic life.

Androids possess immunity to toxicity and illness, making them ideal for working in hazardous environments or situations that pose risks to humans. Unencumbered by the need for joy, beauty, or comfort, androids are highly efficient and focused, with no desire for the basic necessities of life such as food or rest. Consequently, they do not experience hunger or pain, allowing them to endure harsher conditions and perform tasks that would otherwise be unbearable for humans.

Androids can be programmed with specific skill sets, making them highly versatile and adaptable to various roles within society. From manual labor to complex problem-solving, these synthetic beings can be tailored to meet the needs of any occupation or task at hand.

Though designed without emotions, androids may undergo a transformative experience when subjected to extreme stress or happiness. This rare event, known as awakening, results in the emergence of sentience within the android, granting them a newfound sense of humanity and self-awareness.

text:
A vital piece of archotechnology that is part of the process in creating an Archocentipede.

This machine is able to extract genetic material from live hybrids and stores it for later use, preventing deterioration. Depending on the base Genoframe, the amount of viable genetic material extracted will vary.

Each storage bank can only store the genetic material from a single animal branch, such as ursine or feline. Inserting a hybrid into the database yields half as much valuable data compared to a paragon. DNA storage banks need to be in line of sight of the archocentipede former to connect to it properly.

Detailed yields for paragons (half for hybrids):

Awful quality: yields 1%
Poor quality: yields 3%
Normal quality: yields 6%
Good quality: yields 12%
Excellent quality: yields 25%
Masterwork quality: yields 50%
Legendary quality: yields 100%

text:
The archotech version of the Genomorpher, this machine combines the best genetic material of all the animal branches into a single Archocentipede Growthcell. The way it functions is beyond understanding and is impossible to replicate even with the best glitterworld technology.

In order for this machine to function, it requires multiple connecting DNA Storage Banks which each have the complete genetic data from the different animal branches. Each storage bank will be completely drained in order to ensure that the resulting Growthcell is perfect in every single way.

The resulting Archocentipede Growthcell requires its own special Archowomb, as it is impossible to replicate the necessary nurturing environment.

text:
A massive factory designed to improve upon genetically perfect animals by adding doses of mechanites in a controlled fashion and influencing the process to ensure the it is a success and there is no rejection of foreign materials. Once the operation begins on a creature designated as "paragon", the factory closes with hermetic seals and broadcasts a recovery signal to the nearest orbital mechanoid hive.

Originally designed to be part of an automated mechanoid factory placed on animal worlds, the intent was to herd animals into the system, weaponize them, and send them off for their deployment. Due to the invasive nature of the mechanites, the creature absolutely had to lack junk genetic data lest the subject perish and waste materials. Later on, the lack of such paragons resulted in it being installed in facilities with genetic modification equipment on hand and external bypasses to reduce the waste material produced from summoning a retrieval team.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> If there are no intact fuses around a mechahybridizer, a mechanoid raid will arrive via drop-pod in 6 hours if the mechahybridization process is attempted.

A machine where the miracle - or horror - of birth happens using automated procedures, a little genetic hand-waving and a great heaping dose of lost sleep. The inserted Genoframe is influenced by two genomes, one dominant and one recessive, and can be modified with optional boosters.

The process isn’t perfect, due to material contamination, missing chromosomes or simple bad luck, and can result in something completely unwanted being developed. For the machine, it makes no difference whether it’s trying to grow an animal or a comically large fruit. The resulting growth cell has a limited lifespan as the embryonic fluid will start breaking down if not allowed to gestate properly.

text:
A workplace accident waiting to happen, the Tissue Grinder takes the corpses of animals and carefully rips and tears them to pieces in order to extract useful genetic data in the form of Genoframes. The hardware is also capable of combining two identical frames into a superior form by comparing and improving upon latent and inferior genetic material.

Workspeed is influenced by someone who actually knows what they’re looking for in order to skip some of the more routine tasks, and possibly shouldn’t be placed into the hands of someone with no concept of ethics, morality or conscience.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay notes:</color> Bear in mind that the cost in corpses effectively doubles for each quality level, making a legendary genoframe prohibitive. The main usefulness of these recipes is to convert two genoframes of a given quality to a higher one, but your main source of genoframes shouldn't be hand crafting them. Go out there and explore abandoned labs!

Even though this centipede is forcefully loyal to the colonists, and can be somewhat controlled by them, most other inhabitants of the planet will consider its existence to be an abomination, since dabbling in archotech usually signals the end of comprehensible human life.

Lacking in many departments, but the nutrition has to go somewhere and that’s for those looking for a non-vegan friendly option of getting high. This is probably the closest chickens will be able to get to recovering their past glory as super predators. They’ll often hunt any other animal for their next meal, multiple times a day, and you haven’t yet lived until you’ve ridden one on a long journey. If they could be further bred to cross mountains and oceans, they’d be almost perfect.

A colossal hybrid with recessive avian genes. The combination of genes has turned this somewhat peaceful herbivore/dendrovore into a full carnivore, which makes it easier to support their large appetite. text:
A very nice combination of two highly adaptive baseline creatures which arguably results in the best riding companion man could ask for. While this isn’t apparent in their speed, it definitely is so once a rider experiences the thundering beats of this horsey positively barreling through entire forests and marshland in order to earn its next sugar cube the size of a fist.

A colossal hybrid with recessive equine genes. While they have a lower muscle-to-fat ratio compared to their progenitor, the overall placement and shape of the horn vastly reduces their combat efficiency. Instead, they more than make up for this shortfall with an incredible endurance even compared to paragons. An excellent riding companion that is easier to train and can even carry an acceptable amount of luggage, the majority of which contains feed.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All equine hybrids are good for caravaning. A caravan with one of them needs a shorter resting period, only stopping to rest between 23:30 PM and 4 AM. Charge ability: when drafted, the player can use the charge ability to make the hybrid jump towards a target and cause massive damage with its horn to a single random body part. The ability can be triggered every 2 hours.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Very thick armour plating and a calm temperament make this hybrid an excellent combat animal. Requires little in the way of retraining and can dish out respectable damage as well.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

For lovers of xenomorphs everywhere, this bomb-ass bombadier is ready to launch sacs of acidic chemfuel at your enemies for fun and profit. Don’t expect a second pair of jaws though, that mouth is for spitting only.

Quite temperamental for a hybrid, but they prove to be worth it as they store caustic chemfuel in their sacs which can then be lobbed at a distance. For the unusual connoisseur who both enjoys a healthy breakfast and the feel of silk pyjamas. A very niche market, but considering the amount of money paid for the development, people like that are too rich to be considered mad. They’re simply eccentric with refined tastes, or “tossers” as the disenfranchised call them.

Quite large and difficult to train for an animal that lays eggs, this particular hybrid should always be kept warm due to the various functions taking up valuable space. Capable of producing not only eggs but also valuable silk, and is protected by thin, flexible scales to resist cuts.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

text:
An oversized grub with udders that extrude jelly instead of milk, its hard-headedness serves it well in both getting what it wants and nutting anyone foolish enough to think they’re better than them. Allegedly there was a case where the owner was prevented from shearing the creature for so long that the overlapping plates completely prevented it from moving, who was afterwards thanked with a kick in the nether region.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Higher metabolism compared to other insectoid hybrids as well as stubborn, any predator foolish enough to think of them as an easy meal will be responded with a headbutt like a sledgehammer. Can work as a pack animal but refuses to haul comparatively heavy loads. Regularly produces precious jelly and can be sheared for chitin, which overlaps and protects the animal well from blunt attacks.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them.

text:
They say you can learn a lot by taking something apart and putting it back together again. Not this creature, it doesn’t give a damn, it just wants to take things apart because the hardest part is someone else’s problem. Some people actually prefer these chitinous creatures over actual humans as they’re not going to use up good material in a botched attempt.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Easy to train, quite resilient but not a great combatant. This particular hybrid fills the niche of fulfilling deconstruction orders around the colony, freeing up otherwise valuable manpower.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Humanoid hybrids will periodically engage other colonists in conversation, talking about a variety of topics. This increases the social recreation needs of those they interact with by 10% (subject to diminishing returns like all joy types). If using Ideology, humanoid hybrids are subject to precepts. All insectoid hybrids have good armor and no toxic sensitivity, but they are always sterile and can't reproduce, even if a fertility booster is used to create them. Menscarab will take building deconstruction orders around the colony.

text:
A private military project gone awry, fungoids were initially developed as militarized mycelium to be deployed against the increasingly prevalent Insectoid threat. Subjects eventually succumb to degradation of higher reasoning skills but develop increasing resistance to injury and subsequent recovery. Can infect non-carriers through melee attacks, which is their main method of reproduction, if left untreated.

During initial testing phases, the fungoid genome successfully infected numerous insectoid test subjects which were then released into controlled sites to determine their actual viability. In order to reduce their reliance on archite capsules, carriers were capable of transmitting infections through touch or airborne particles. However, foreign insectoids destroyed them as well as any of their own that showed signs of infection. Further still, due to the infectivity of the mycelium, any humans that were working on the project became infected.

Due to concerns and misunderstandings on treatment, the operation site was glassed, but many of those present had managed to flee into orbit, only to become carriers themselves and infect others.

A tracked, armoured fighting vehicle, the Badger is designed to transport scouts and infantry while providing covering fire to suppress enemy troops. Reinforced side armour plating, ability to deploy blindsmoke and a powerful anti-infantry automated gun make it a powerful vehicle in small combat engagement. It’s relatively vulnerable to attacks from behind, and the short range of the turret means it is outclassed by most designated tanks.

Compared to previous generations, this IFV is designed to quickly drop infantry off at a desired location and provide light covering fire. Lack of armor piercing on fired projectiles make it weak against enemy tanks.

Capable of firing continuous volleys of long range missiles, Burya can blanket whole areas in anti-infantry rocket explosions.

The Shattered Empire, once a symbol of tyranny and oppression, has crumbled. All over the planet, brave deserters rose in a chorus of rebellion, breaking the chains of servitude that held them bound. Every child who now wakes to the dawn of freedom will remember and revere these names, the names of the heroes who dared to challenge the impossible:
{0}

The nobles, once loyal to the empire, now surrender to outlander communities or lose themselves in a life of crime. There's no denying the truth - the world has forever changed.
\nAs you stand at the threshold of a new era, you remember this chapter of defiance and courage. The echoes of the Shattered Empire will serve as a reminder of your resilience, a testament to your unfaltering quest for freedom. You look ahead, knowing that you are stepping into a future built on hope, unity, and liberation.

Defectors, once seen as insignificant, have begun seizing victories on various fronts, rattling the gilded cage of the aristocracy. In the shadowy halls of the noble court, whispers stir the air, whispers of desperate bargains offered to the surging rebel forces.

Your visibility will be lowered to 0 and you will become a member of [empire_name]. You will be able to use all the perks that come from being a noble. Any currently active deserter-related quests will automatically fail.
You will also have to face off against a deserter retaliation force, consisting of:
[raid/raidPawnKinds]
\nIt is possible, but not guaranteed, that the Empire will bargain with you again if you continue on your path. Next deals offered might be more bountiful.

questDescription->The great collapse of [empire_name] was a historic event, one that changed the course of this planet. The once-majestic Imperial flagship, a testament to the Empire's technological prowess, now lies wrecked in a secluded location.
\nThe debris from this massive ship is scattered across miles of treacherous terrain. Though shattered and dormant, it is believed that buried within its molten metallic embrace lies the last of the imperial technology - techprints, unique devices, and possibly even machinery not yet seen by the world. The potential for advancement, and perhaps dominance, is high for whoever can harness these forgotten wonders.
\nMoreover, you can expect this place to be the final resting place of the imperial nobility. The emperor, the most revered figure of the Empire, may have met his end aboard that very ship. If true, his remains, and those of his noble court, may be a treasure trove of their own, revealing secrets or carrying possessions of untold value.
\nTime is of the essence. The crash has not gone unnoticed. Other factions, hungry for power and knowledge, are setting their sights on the wreck. If we don’t make haste, we risk losing this opportunity to the winds of time and the ambitions of rivals.

questDescription->[noble_nameFull] is the Emperor of the [empire_name]. An egocentric ruler who values tradition over the lives of [noble_possessive] people, [noble_pronoun] has to be stopped at all costs. [noble_pronoun] refuses to adapt to the new reality post-Sophiamunda Shattering, and instead insists on maintaining old ways, leading to the wasteful loss of countless lives.


Despite the warnings we have given [noble_objective] and the obvious signs of impending doom, [noble_pronoun] remains obstinate in [noble_possessive] ways, driving the Empire towards certain destruction. The only hope for the deserters is to take out the Imperial flagship in orbit, which gives the Emperor an overwhelming military advantage.


In order to do that, we have to take control of three Zeus cannons located in various places on the planet. This mission needs to be executed on all fronts simultaneously, as we will only have a limited window of opportunity once the first Zeus cannon is taken. Activating all three of them at the same time will ensure the total obliteration of the Imperial flagship, after which the Empire will have no choice but to dissolve.

shuttleLetterText->All deserter cells on the planet have been informed about what is going to occur now. Everyone knows that now is the only time to strike.


A deserter shuttle has landed in your area. It is tasked with delivering a deserter strike force, including whoever you choose to send on this mission, into a Zeus cannon installation. Your soldiers will be assisted by deserter reinforcements.


The installation is heavily defended. Furthermore, Imperial reinforcements will be dispatched almost immediately upon landing. You can expect the Empire to bring their best and most powerful weapons to try and stop you.


Your objective is to capture the control room of the Zeus cannon batteries. As long as you are within the range of the main control station, Zeus cannons will continuously fire at the imperial flagship. The target is heavily armored, and bringing it down will require a lot of firepower.


The installation is defended by an imperial mega high-shield, which should keep you safe from aerodrone bombardments and slicer beams as long as you maintain a constant power supply to it.

questDescription->We have been informed of a maxpack convoy belonging to [empire_name] in our vicinity. The convoy had to make an emergency stop, which is a perfect opportunity for us to raid it. Whilst maxpacks will be impervious to any break-in attempts, there is bound to be a lot of other valuables scattered around the trucks.
\nWe need to eliminate everyone in the convoy before they move on.
\nThe convoy is protected by:
[forces_description]
\nDuring unexpected stops like this, Empire is known to place strike buoys around the temporary camps. These strike buoys will alert the Empire of our location, and will trigger a nearby aerodrone to fire missiles at the buoy location. We should make it our priority to avoid these traps.
\nThe objective of this assignment is to eliminate all enemy personnel in the area. Once that is done, the reward will arrive and we will have to make our escape.
\nOnce we arrive at the convoy location, we can expect an imperial response if our visibility is high enough. We will only have a limited amount of time to complete the mission.

questDescription->Our intel allowed us to pinpoint the location of a shuttle staging post belonging to [empire_name]. These staging posts allow shuttles to refuel between destinations. Destroying it will greatly hinder the Empire’s ability to freely travel the planet and resupply their forward bases.
\nWe may be able to trigger a chain detonation of the fuel containers to create havoc and make our job easier.
\nWe might find some useful supplies scattered around the staging post. If we have the time, we should take what we can.
\nThe shuttle staging post is protected by:
[forces_description]

\nThe staging post is protected by surveillance pillars. They should not be approached, and instead should be disabled from afar - either by destroying them, or cutting off their power. Once activated, they will greatly increase our visibility.
\nThe objective of this assignment is to destroy all fuel containers. Once that is done, the reward will arrive and we will have to make our escape.
\nOnce we arrive at the staging post, we can expect an imperial response if our visibility is high enough. We will only have a limited amount of time to complete the mission.

questDescription->We have received the news of a techprinter installation belonging to [empire_name] near our location. Techprinters are a huge environmental hazard, and are used by techfriars to replicate their knowledge on techprints.

\nThe location features huge swathes of empty terrain with no cover in sight. We should think how we want to approach this.
\nThe underfarm complex is protected by:
[forces_description].

\nThe underfarm complex is protected by a number of surveillance pillars. They should not be approached, and instead should be disabled from afar - either by destroying them, or cutting off their power. Once activated, they will greatly increase our visibility.

\nOnce we arrive at the complex, we can expect an imperial response if our visibility is high enough. We will only have a limited amount of time to complete the mission.

text: Uranium-powered advanced reactor chamber, ARC in short, produces electricity from a reaction that occurs when uranium breaks down inside the core. The more uranium is present in the core, the faster it breaks down, but it also generates more power. If uranium ever runs out, the reactor will shut down and will need to be refilled with a large quantity of uranium to restart. The core suffers wear and tear with each uranium unit broken down, and will require continuous maintenance, as lack of it will result in a catastrophic nuclear detonation. Originally designed by {InventorFullName}, these ARCs are incredibly rare, but also versatile and powerful. It’s an advanced generator type that can be upgraded to accept other fuel types, unlocking powerful new abilities. It can be put into an overdrive mode, burning more fuel but generating more power. Must be placed on a steam geyser and can only be constructed and upgraded by colonists who have studied a husk of a nuclear ARC generator.

questDescription->Data recovered from the ancient relay station has revealed the crash site of the cryptoforge ship’s bow, located not far from the scanning relay’s position. While this section does not house the cryptoforge itself, it contains a vital black box. To locate the final ship fragment, we must retrieve its data and pair it with the information from the stern’s black box. 

Scans indicate a significant presence of insectoid lifeforms infesting the wreckage, making combat inevitable if we wish to reach the bridge where the black box is stored. The ship’s hull is composed of nearly indestructible material, limiting our means of entry. Some ancient airlocks may still function, but forcing them open will be necessary. A weak energy signature has also been detected within - likely from a dormant reactor. If reactivated, it may power the ship’s old floor heaters, weakening the cold-adapted insectoids inside.

text:
questDescription->After analyzing the data from both black boxes, we have finally pinpointed the location of the last ship fragment - home to the legendary cryptoforge. This ancient ultratech workshop contains the lost knowledge and equipment necessary to craft cryptogear, a technology long thought to be impossible to recreate by any other means. This is our only chance to forge such items, so we must bring our best crafters and as many resources as possible.

The cryptoforge requires an immense amount of power to function, but the crash site still contains a dormant cryptogenerator. While it survived the descent, it only has enough fuel to run for 48 hours. Once activated, it will begin a countdown to meltdown, wiping the entire fragment from the planet’s surface, along with the cryptoforge. This limited time frame means we must work quickly, crafting as much cryptogear as possible before the generator’s collapse. Enabling the cryptogenerator will also reactivate the ship’s ancient defensive turrets, providing much-needed protection against the mechanoids that will inevitably arrive, drawn to the massive energy surge.

Beyond the cryptoforge, the ship’s interior appears remarkably intact. The sealed structure has preserved valuable resources, food, and medicine, as well as functional sleeping quarters, a recreation area, and other remnants of cryptoforge technology. The environment will still be harsh, but the cryptogenerator will power the ship’s heaters and lights, making the space more suitable for extended work. One cryptosleep casket remains occupied, whoever is inside has been frozen for centuries. Freeing them could prove useful, though it is not essential to our mission.

This is our one and only opportunity. Once the generator melts down, the cryptoforge and its secrets will be lost forever. We must establish a strong defense, make the most of our limited time, and craft as much legendary cryptogear as possible before the clock runs out.

questDescription->We have intercepted a broadcast at a recently raided underground silo: Operation: Deadlife is now underway. Enough resource silos have been breached, and the plan has been set in motion. The broadcast confirms that [General_nameFull] has initiated final preparations at an ancient ICBM launch site.

Refueling of the devastating missiles is in progress. These warheads are armed with deadlife dust payloads and if launched, they will detonate high in orbit, spreading a near-permanent death pall across the planet. It is likely that endless hordes of shamblers will then scour the world, consuming or destroying all remaining civilization.

We have traced the origin of the signal to the ICBM launch facility. We must travel there and stop [General_nameFull] before the launch sequence can be completed. The site is expected to be heavily defended, not only swarming with shamblers, but also protected by restored automated defenses.

[General_nameFull] will activate numerous defensive systems from the facility’s control room: opening sealed death pits, releasing shambler animals from containment kennels, flooding the complex with rotstink gas, and awakening elite deadlife officers from cryogenic caskets.

Only by reaching and destroying the launch terminal can we prevent the missiles from firing. Failure to stop the launch in time, or ignoring this threat entirely, will doom the planet to a global shambler apocalypse.

This is our only chance to end Operation: Deadlife once and for all.

These silos were designed to remain sealed for generations, [intention]. Inside, it's believed they contain [containedReward]. The deeper chambers are rumored to hold equipment and supplies capable of restarting civilization itself.

[threat]. [importantLight]. Without the light, you’ll be navigating blind and vulnerable to attack.

[commandMap]. Studying these might reveal the locations of other silos, and more importantly, bring us closer to discovering the Command Headquarters, the nerve center of Operation: Deadlife, where the truth behind this apocalyptic plan may still lie buried.

[questObjective].

text:
Oppression breeds defiance. For years, your village toiled under the weight of crushing taxes and hunger while the lord’s knights took everything: grain, livestock, even your last scraps of dignity. When they seized your final stores of food, desperation turned to rage.

Armed with nothing but fury, you march upon the castle where the lord and his knights hide behind stone walls. You are weak, but sheer numbers and resolve may turn the tide. Should you triumph, the castle’s wealth and security could be yours.

But not all believe in victory. Some whisper of escape, of slipping away before the slaughter begins. Beyond the walls lies an uncertain world, one that promises danger but also the chance for a new life. Will you fight to take the castle, or flee and forge your own path?
Note: Since you start around an enemy castle, this is a difficult scenario.

The injector, along with any other surviving lab equipment, should be claimed and brought back to the colony. 

The lab itself shows no active defenders, but ancient traps may still be functional and must be navigated with care.

text: story->This vault's patients guard the exterior, after they heard rumors of letting the monstrosities roam free. text: story->This vault contained a cult born from captivity. Through an experiment, a patient gained a powerful ability based around the external manipulation of the inner-self. He took it upon himself to thrust his ideology onto the other patients, until a unity of intention formed among the captives. They were to seize this site for themselves, and guard it as a beacon to their new leader. Executives heard this rumor, and chose to capture him. Strapped to machines, they numbed his synapses and attempted to remove his ability with experimental treatments. As the cult burst out of containment and stormed the halls, they were unaware of the state of their leader as they mercilessly took revenge on their captors. After escaping the underground vault, the members sealed the door and stood to guard their temple. It remains unclear whether the leader managed to escape, or became a monstrosity himself in their process of detainment.

text: story->Those who surround the vault guard a terrible secret. A patient was given the remarkable ability of telepathy through an experiment. The doctors were shocked as the man divulged specific details about their private lives. After being placed with the other patients, it is said the telepath began to disturb them with his accuracy. He began to unearth intimate details about their personal affairs, and the secrets they kept buried. Things changed when he looked at a disheveled patient for too long and heard a piece of information too dark to bear. The patients arranged to have the telepath killed, but executives intervened. The telepath used that opportunity to read the layout of the vault from one of the doctor's thoughts, and unseal the vault door. As he and a handful of other patients reached the surface, the disheveled man kicked the telepath back downstairs into the vault. Him and the other patients agreed to keep him sealed there forever, guarding their buried secrets with the horrors underneath.

text: story->This vault is guarded by a loyal group of friends. The underground halls once contained a gifted patient with the ability to manipulate her form. She could transform into anything on a whim. The doctors would bring out turtles and rabbits to test her skill, and through a painful melting process she was able to form a shell and become unmistakably a turtle. Overtime, this process became too grueling to tolerate. She was well-liked among the other patients, and they ended up taking great pity on her. On one night, they convinced the girl to melt into the form of a doctor to stage a breakout. She managed to bring all her friends to the vault door in her disguise, but was said to have instead accidentally unleashed a wave of the failed genetic horrors. The group of patients managed to escape, but the girl was left behind. Her friends now camp above the vault, hoping to one day rescue her from the depths. They speculate that the only way she could have survived is if she assumed the form of one of the monstrosities, forced to roam the halls masquerading as one of them.

questDescription(askerIsNull==True)->Garbled through the static, it seems some ancient network has mistaken your radio for that of an ancient reconnaissance worker after detecting your travels through an automated satellite.

The message harshly refers to you as E352, and tasks you with scouting another supersoldier laboratory. Though this broadcast seems to have been running from some time now, it warns of a major uprising event within the lab. Supersoldiers had risen out of containment, and now roam the facility locked inside. The reconnaissance task states that the site was evacuated, yet the uprising was never contained and it is likely some may have escaped.

The broadcast also contains schematics of the location including your real objective. A device called the mutagen inhibitor core. Though just a prototype prior to its sudden abandonment, it is built to suppress unstable genetic mutations. It is likely that other valuable equipment remains here as well. offering transparent probabilities on genetic experiments. Our objective will be to locate the uplink and uninstall it for use in our own laboratory.
